        Quick facts

        Facts checked Nov. 9, 2026
        Motors and speed
        No horsepower limit (ODNR).
        Ramps and access
        Three launch ramps: Taylor Rd (campground), Deer Park and Rattlesnake (ODNR).
        Normal pool
        Summer pool is 798 ft, the level the ODNR fishing map is drawn at; the Corps holds 787.5 ft in winter. Live level: Corps of Engineers gauge.
        Night rules
        State park hours are 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.; ODNR allows legitimate recreation, like fishing, outside those hours. Source: ODNR, Paint Creek State Park.

        How to read this
        • Pool is lake surface elevation in feet as the Corps posts it, not the depth of any hole or channel.
        • The ODNR fishing map’s depths are based on the 798 ft normal summer pool (5 ft contours, surveyed 1999). Contours are off by about (798 − pool). The Corps holds the lake near 787.5 ft in winter.
        • Water temp is the Corps outflow reading, labelled outflow. USACE posts it every hour. It is not lake surface temperature, and the bite rating does not use it. USACE Paint Creek Lake.
        • Lake level comes from the Corps of Engineers, Huntington District, every 15 minutes. USACE Paint Creek Lake.
        • Unlimited horsepower (ODNR). No paddlefish may be taken in the lake or within 2,000 ft of it and the dam (2026–27 rules).

        Tonight’s bite

        A rule of thumb guide, not a promise.

        How the bite is rated

        The Bite is this site’s own rule of thumb, not fishing science and not a forecast. It adds points from readings already on this page.

        • Barometer, the change over the last 3 hours at the lake’s NWS station. Falling slowly +2, steady +1, rising slowly 0, falling fast 0, rising fast −1. Steady means within 0.02 inHg; fast means 0.06 inHg or more.
        • Wind, tonight’s average NWS hourly speed from sunset to 2 AM (the top of each hour’s range). Under 3 mph 0, 3 to 12 mph +1, 13 to 18 mph 0, over 18 mph −2.
        • Moon, worked out on this phone. New or full moon tonight (or under 10% or over 90% lit) +1, otherwise 0.
        • Water temp, from this lake’s USGS gauge where one reports it. 55 to 80°F +1, colder than 45 or warmer than 86°F −1, anything between 0. It never makes a rating alone.
        • Thunder anywhere in tonight’s NWS forecast makes it Tough, whatever the points.

        4 points or more is Good, 2 or 3 is Fair, less is Tough. A missing reading counts 0, and with no barometer trend and no wind there is no rating.

              • Unofficial Ohio fishing hub with night-dock atmosphere: Hoover, Alum Creek, Buckeye Lake, O’Shaughnessy, Griggs, Indian Lake, Delaware Lake, Deer Creek Lake, Madison Lake, Knox Lake, Clear Fork Reservoir, Seneca Lake, Dillon Lake, Lake Logan, Salt Fork Lake, Burr Oak Lake, Dow Lake, Mosquito Creek Lake, Berlin Lake, West Branch Reservoir, Pymatuning Lake, Lake Milton, Leesville Lake, Grand Lake St. Marys, Caesar Creek Lake, East Fork Lake, C.J. Brown Reservoir, Rocky Fork Lake, LaDue Reservoir, Paint Creek Lake, Portage Lakes, Mogadore Reservoir, Lake Loramie, Nimisila Reservoir, Cowan Lake, Acton Lake, Tappan Lake, Piedmont Lake, Clendening Lake, Atwood Lake, Charles Mill Lake, Pleasant Hill Lake and Beach City Lake
              • Species pages with limit reminders from the ODNR 2026–27 rules
              • One example log entry, marked Example · not ODNR / City / USGS
              Night fishing can be dangerous in storms, heat, and low visibility. Wear a life jacket when it calls for it. Unlimited hp · crappie 30 a day, 9 in minimum · bass 4 a day split · license ages 16+. See About.
